note: Mutants judged equivalent (no test could tell them from the original), recorded by `file:line:col mutator → replacement` as SURVIVORS.md prints them, never by Stryker's unstable ids. Each entry is {"mutant": "<that key>", "original": "<the source text the mutant replaces, as it reads at line:col>", "line": "<that whole source line, trimmed>", "reason": "<why no test can distinguish it, at least 10 characters>"}; the original and the line pin the key to the code it was judged on (a short original such as `""` repeats on other lines), so a key a line shift has moved onto different code is refused (test/stryker-floor.test.ts) instead of excusing another mutant. A recorded mutant leaves the denominator of its group's score; the wave that owns the file records it, after reading the code.

buildTimetable's `mode` only picks keyOf's branch: "" equals neither "per_pitch" nor "per_division", so it takes the same last branch (one unnamed group) as "auto"; mode is read nowhere else.
buildRoster's default only feeds `=== "per_team"`, and "" is as much not "per_team" as "auto" is; the value is read nowhere else.
buildOfficialsRota's default only feeds `=== "per_team"`, and "" is as much not "per_team" as "auto" is; the value is read nowhere else.

Page groups are sorted with localeCompare, so a "" group (auto, or fixtures with no division) always sorts first and its first section is pushed while sections.length is 0: the break's `group !== ""` conjunct never decides it, whatever it compares against.

twoSidedBracket puts the first half of every pre-final round on L and the second half on R, so col 0 holds as many R nodes as L; a centre node sits at col 0 only in a one-round (2-entrant) field, where L counts 0, the mutant 1, and Math.max(1, ·) makes both 1.

Dropping the null short-circuit leaves `!scope.poolIds.includes(f.poolId)`. poolIds is a string[] (ClearScope: z.array(z.string()); the same type on every caller), which never holds null, so a pool-less fixture still reads includes(null) = false and is skipped exactly as `f.poolId === null` skipped it; for a pooled fixture the operand was false already.

Dropping the null short-circuit leaves `!scope.rounds.includes(f.roundNo)`. rounds is a number[] (ClearScope: z.array(z.number().int())), which never holds null, so a round-less fixture still reads includes(null) = false and is skipped exactly as `f.roundNo === null` skipped it; for a fixture with a round the operand was false already.

Dropping the null short-circuit leaves `!scope.courts.includes(f.court)`. courts is a string[] (ClearScope: z.array(z.string())), which never holds null, so a court-less fixture still reads includes(null) = false and is skipped exactly as `f.court === null` skipped it; for a fixture on a court the operand was false already.

A key's version Map is never empty: byKey is private to createRegistry's closure, register() is its only writer and calls byKey.set only after versions.set has put the module in, and SportRegistry has no unregister or delete. So the operand is false in every reachable state and `false` in its place changes nothing; an unknown key is refused by `!versions`, which the mutant keeps.

`>= 0` differs from `> 0` only when compareSemver returns 0, i.e. two DIFFERENT version strings that parse to the same triple. The version Map is keyed by the exact string and register() refuses a duplicate, and parseSemver refuses leading zeros (semver.org §2), so each (major, minor, patch) has exactly one spelling: two keys in the Map never compare equal, and the module being compared is never `best` itself because `best` is taken from earlier iterations. With `>=` the replacement would only differ on a tie, which cannot occur.
